names.official: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

summary: São Tomé and Príncipe exempts citizens of the EU, the US, Canada and the Portuguese-speaking CPLP countries from visas under Law 5/2015, and the UK, US and Canadian governments give their citizens 15 days visa-free. The law also exempts nationals of countries with visa-abolition agreements and of third countries set by decree, but neither list is published, so for other nationalities no official source we could read states the rule; visas are applied for online on the Migration and Border Service's eVisa portal before arrival.

conditionalWaivers.text: Law 5/2015 (article 25(1)(f) of the Foreigners Act) lets citizens of any other country enter without a visa if they hold a passport valid for more than three months and a valid Schengen or United States visa, and their planned stay does not exceed fifteen days.

passportValidity.text: eVisa applicants upload a passport valid for at least three months beyond the last day of stay the visa allows. The FCDO tells visa-free British visitors only that the passport must be valid for the whole stay.

notes: The UK FCDO says there are severe penalties for all drug offences: pack your luggage yourself and do not carry anything through customs for anyone else.

safety.text: Canada advises taking normal security precautions in São Tomé and Príncipe. It says petty crime such as pickpocketing and bag-snatching occurs, particularly in markets, on beaches and on busy streets near hotels, and that violent crime is rare but does occur.

tips.text: The UK, US and Canadian governments give their citizens a visa-free stay of 15 days, and the exemption law sets no other length. For a longer stay, ask the Migration and Border Service for an extension.

The UK FCDO says cards are not widely accepted and ATMs are few, and Canada says foreign bank cards cannot be used to withdraw money from ATMs and that banks exchange US dollars, euros and CFA francs.

Canada's travel advice says malaria is a risk in São Tomé and Príncipe and that antimalarial medication is recommended for most travellers — see a health professional before you go and use insect repellent.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU, the US, Canada and the Portuguese-speaking CPLP countries are exempt from visas under Law 5/2015. The UK government says British visitors need no visa for up to 15 days, and the US and Canadian governments give their citizens the same 15 days; the law itself sets no length of stay. The law also exempts nationals of countries with visa-abolition agreements and of third countries set by decree, but neither list is published, so for other nationalities no official source we could read states the rule. Visas are applied for online on the Migration and Border Service (SMF) e-visa portal before arrival.

faq.question: How can I stay longer than 15 days?
faq.answer: Ask the Migration and Border Service in São Tomé for an extension: under Law 5/2008 (article 43), visitors admitted without a visa can be given up to 30 days more, renewable once for the same period.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: The UK government says you need a yellow fever certificate if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

faq.question: What money should I bring to São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says credit cards are not widely accepted and ATMs are few; Canada says foreign bank cards cannot be used at ATMs and that banks exchange US dollars, euros and Central African CFA francs.
